figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the proposed DTW-GBC framework. DTW is first used to compute pairwise distances between training time series, with the DTW distance matrix and optimal warping path for one sample pair illustrated on the left. These pairwise distances are then used to recursively organize the training samples into granular balls, as illustrated on the right, for subsequent granular-ball-level nearest-neighbor classification.
Table 2: Candidate values of κ on the DTW-GBC-R for each dataset.
Figure 2: The average numbers of 1-NN comparisons per test sample corresponding to the best performances for each method reported in Tables 3 and 4, respectively.
Table 3: Classification performances on four datasets with η = 0.1.
Table 4: Classification performances on four datasets with η = 0.2.
Figure 3: The average weighted G-mean and average number of generated granular balls of DTW-GBC-R and DTWGBC-L under different ρ on four benchmark datasets with η = 0.1 (upper) and η = 0.2 (bottom).
